title: SSE session reauthorize and lossy-replay mitigation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Scope: Implement a defensible reauthorization handshake and lossy-replay mitigation for SSE streaming clients that may reconnect across rolling model swaps or control-plane restarts. Goal is to avoid silent data gaps or duplicate function-calls when sessions reattach to a different backend instance or model variant; preserve ordered semantic continuity where possible and fail fast with clear diagnostics when continuity cannot be guaranteed.

This ticket covers protocol, server-side token semantics, client hints, and observability. It does NOT include implementing new client SDKs (those will be follow-up tasks), but must expose clear backward-compatible HTTP/SSE headers and status codes that SDKs can adopt incrementally.

Constraints & assumptions:
- Many clients are browser-based consuming SSE; others are server-side long pollers.
- We cannot require long-lived symmetric secrets for tokens; solution must work with short-lived session leases and reauth flow via standard bearer reissue endpoints.
- Model hot-swap and rolling restarts occur frequently on Dedicated/private tenants; reconnects across different model variants are common.

Non-goals:
- Full end-to-end client SDK changes.
- Changing function-call payload schemas or tool contract semantics (we ensure idempotency boundaries instead).
acceptance_criteria: Server accepts a reconnect attempt carrying a session micro-checkpoint token and validates it against a short-lived lease; if valid, the server resumes stream with 'resume-point' metadata and no duplicate tool/function-call events
If resume is impossible (e.g., model changed incompatibly or server lost buffer), server returns a structured SSE 'resume_failed' event with reauth hint and a deterministic reason code
Clients can opt into optimistic reconnect (resume if possible) or strict restart (reject resume) via the 'Prefer' request header; behavior is documented in the API reference
All reauthorize/reconcile transitions emit structured telemetry: resume.requests, resume.success, resume.failure.reason=[auth|incompatible_model|evicted|buffer_lost], and token_refresh_count
No silent duplicate function-call invocations occur in our internal canary runs across 10k reconnects; observed duplicate rate = 0% for covered flows
New SSE response metadata fields are backward-compatible: unknown fields are ignored by older clients and do not break the stream
notes: 2026-03-01 - Ava Chen: Created ticket after incident IN-2026-02 where a control-plane restart during a Dedicated model-roll caused duplicate function-call side effects for 3 customers. Root cause: server resumed streams without validating model-compatibility of cached function-call checkpoints.

2026-03-03 - Marcus Patel: Spike complete. Prototyped micro-checkpoint token format (opaque nonce + lease_id; server keeps ephemeral mapping in redis with TTL). Decided against embedding full checkpoint in token to avoid token bloat and cross-region replication delay.

2026-03-04 - Marcus Patel: Trade-off discussion with Research: We can attempt transparent in-memory rehydration of KV cache for resuming sessions, but that creates cross-instance dependencies. Decision: allow resume only when the server instance can assert checkpoint provenance; otherwise return resume_failed with reason 'evicted' to prompt client re-request. Recording in design doc.

2026-03-05 - Design review (Sofia López): Requested a clear UX for 'resume_failed' including suggested client actions (reauth, reissue request with same prompt, or fallback to non-streaming). Added requirement to include deterministic reason codes and link to Troubleshooting KB.

2026-03-06 - Security review (Eli Rosen): Concern about replayable tokens. Agreed to add single-use lease_id and rotate token upon successful resume; include origin binding (client_id) when possible. Marked security_review_required = true.

2026-03-07 - Marcus Patel: Implemented server changes in runtime PR. Key behaviors: accept 'X-Resume-Token' header containing base64(lease_id:nonce:signature). On validation, server emits an SSE control event 'resume_point' with sequence number and last-ack checksum. If incompatible model, server sends 'resume_failed' event and 410-style SSE end segment.

2026-03-08 - QA (Nina Gupta): Integration tests added for three scenarios: successful resume on same model instance, resume rejected due to incompatible model hash, and resume rejected due to expired lease. Tests run against canary cluster. Observed transient 0.01% race where token rotated while reconnect inflight; added server-side 2s grace window for lease rotation.

2026-03-09 - Observability (Jamal Price): Dashboard added: Resume Attempts / minute, Resume Success %, Failure reasons breakdown, and Duplicate Function-Call alerts. Hooked into existing tracing span 'sse.resume' with tags for customer_id and model_variant. Link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/streaming/resume-metrics

2026-03-10 - Marcus Patel: Rolling canary deploy started for runtime-1.24 on 5% of traffic. Early metrics: resume.success = 87% (expected), resume.failure.incompatible_model = 9%, resume.failure.evicted = 3%, duplicates observed = 0 in first 12h. Next: expand canary and prepare SDK guidance note for JS and Python clients.
